  "text": "By spring the harbour office needed painting. Maren bought two tins of blue and found, when she opened them, that they were different blues. She used the darker one on the door.

Erris came after school to help. She painted the lower boards carefully, then less carefully, and left a thumbprint beside the latch.

Maren let it dry.

There were things her mother had left that were not instructions. A chipped cup. A receipt for pears. A photograph of herself standing beside a bus, laughing at someone outside the frame. Maren put the photograph on the kitchen shelf. For years it had lain face down in a drawer because there was nobody left to name the place.

Now she thought the place might not matter.

That evening she made enough soup for two and took half to Erris's grandmother. Coming back, she saw the new blue door from across the harbour. It looked almost bright.

At midnight she put on her coat.

The duty had not grown smaller. There were evenings when she stood with one arm in a sleeve and could not bear the thought of the stairs. Then she put in the other arm.

Tonight there was a pear in her pocket. She had meant to eat it after supper.

After the three turns, she sat on the top step and ate it slowly. Below her, a boat knocked against its fender. Someone crossed the harbour road carrying bread beneath a coat.

She wrapped the core in her handkerchief and went down before the juice dried on her fingers."
